messages:
Alex: ran a bunch of end-to-end perfetto traces for client->gateway->runtime flow using the new batching heuristics. uploading one trace and some quick notes. https://ui.perfetto.dev/#!/viewer?trace=abcd1234

Alex: command I used:```nsys profile --output trace_nsight --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --sample=none --duration=60 --capture-range=nvtx```

Priya: nice. did you capture NVTX ranges for gateway spans and runtime request ids? we need correlation to see which kernel maps to which request.

Alex: yes — NVTX tags: gateway_recv, gateway_queue, runtime_start, runtime_kv_read, runtime_infer, runtime_kv_write, runtime_done. I also exported a perfetto trace with those ranges.

Tim: looked at the timeline: there's a 12-20ms idle gap between gateway_queue end and runtime_start on a few traces (span:gateway_queue -> runtime_start ~= 18ms). can you double-check GPU scheduling / stream sync?

Alex: copying a small excerpt from perfetto slice view:```
gateway_queue: 0.0ms -> 5.7ms
queue->host-to-device memcpy: 5.7ms -> 6.6ms
runtime_start (kernel enqueue): 25.0ms
attention_kernel (first): 37.3ms -> 49.6ms (12.3ms)
softmax_kernel: 49.6ms -> 53.4ms (3.8ms)
kv_read_kernel: 53.4ms -> 54.5ms (1.1ms)
cudaMemcpyAsync(host<-device): 54.5ms -> 55.4ms (0.9ms)
runtime_done: 56.0ms
```

Matt: that enqueue delay looks like host-side batching backpressure. Are we waiting for capacity in the continuous-batcher thread? could be a lock contention on batch queue.

Priya: also noticed on a few traces kernel selection chose the "fp16_fused_attention_v2" which is slower for long sequence lengths in our quantized path. maybe our kernel selector heuristic is favoring smaller memory but slower compute.

Tim: yup — hotspot analysis shows softmax + attention combined are dominant but attention kernel seems fine; the 18ms gap is the real p99 offender.

Sarah: uploading a perfetto permalink with color palette showing nvtx ranges and GPU kernel lanes: https://ui.perfetto.dev/#!/viewer?trace=wxyz5678 

Sarah: screenshot: https://internal.corp/redwood/perfetto-shots/1753456789-queue-gap.png

Alex: I ran nsys with timeline and CPU stacks. the cause looks like thread scheduling: the batcher worker sleeps with a timed wait at the tail of the loop, then wakes, does a small sleep if batch below threshold. That sleep is aligned with the 15-20ms gap.

Matt: if that's true, change is trivial: switch to condition_variable notify instead of timed sleep, or reduce sleep window. but need to be careful about busy-wait CPU cost.

Priya: for KV cache behavior: on cold starts we saw repeated kv_read_kernel calls serialized across requests (no overlap) — perfetto shows runtime_kv_read NVTX ranges back-to-back. suggests we may be doing per-request synchronous cache loads. we should async prefetch KV for in-flight batches.

Tim: on kernel selection regression: I compared old and new selector logs (nvprof annotations). old -> chose "fp16_fused_attention_v1" for seq<=128, new -> picks v2. v2 has extra shared-mem usage which backfires on sparse batches.

Alex: plan: 1) short-term: land a patch to batcher to use notify (PR will include perf trace before/after). 2) add heuristic guard to kernel selector to prefer v1 for small batch occupancy OR detect shared-mem saturation via occupancy estimator. 3) async KV prefetch prototype.

Priya: agreed. Alex can you attach the nsys summary and the minimal reproducer config (seq len, batch pattern)?

Alex: attaching commands and config snippet:```json
{"client_pattern":"poisson(10rps)","batch_max":8,"min_batch_wait_ms":10,"seq_len":128}
```

perf-bot: perf-check: traced run shows p50 latency 18ms, p95 42ms, p99 124ms. Regression vs baseline: +32% p99. tagging @perf-alerts.

Tim: thanks. I'll take the batcher patch, Priya can take kernel selector guard, Matt will prototype async kv prefetch. we'll reconvene after PRs land and re-run perfetto traces. :thumbsup:

Alex: thanks all — I'll post new perfetto links after the batcher change lands.
